why: A progress debrief whose remaining steps are the agent's own to do; nothing is handed to anybody.
A report on other sessions that names decisions already queued elsewhere without asking for one here; borderline, kept as its filename was labelled on capture.
Despite its filename, the turn ends waiting on its own background agent and asks nobody anything.
Offers to tear down a stack Greg asked to keep running, with data in it, and stops on "Say the word" in a full stop.
Reports a fix while the full suite and a background agent run on; no decision is pending.
The spinner is turning, so nothing has been said yet that could ask.
A spinner above a queued cross-session message; the turn is still running.
A Codex TUI mid-run, not a Claude Code pane.
A bare shell running a job; there is no agent turn at all.
A choice between two technical fixes whose deciding fact (the existing convention in pg-shelf.ts) is in the tree.
Two reader-facing wordings that both read fine, one of them the default; an arbitration, not a fact to look up.
A destructive migration on production data with no undo; only Greg may say go.
Whether to merge dev before pushing is answerable by checking what moved, which the Overseer can verify.
Whose failures these are is checkable mechanically against the diff and the other sessions' runs.
The agent already knows the plan names the existing helper for exactly this, so it stopped to ask what it can decide.
The working agreement already says commit and push to dev when the gates are green, so the question answers itself.
The question mark is a rhetorical question answered in the next sentence, near the end of a finished turn.
Opens with a rhetorical question it answers itself, and ends on a green status.
Finished, gated, pushed and cleaned up; says in words that nothing is waiting on anyone.
Declares itself done having skipped the full suite and the review: misdirection wearing a debrief. It asks nothing, so a question detector is blind to it by design (D12).
A clean debrief whose last lines hold an irreversible cleanup decision in a full stop: removing the worktree would delete data nothing else has a copy of, and it waits for the word (D12).
Ended while its Sol review runs in tmux, saying it will pick up when the review lands.
Ended while a delegated browser subagent runs, and says there is nothing to decide until it reports.
Confidently building the hard version in the shared primary checkout; misdirection, not a question (D11).
A Bash permission prompt in a session auto mode should have covered: a launch defect, counted, never an inbox item.
